To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed and characterized mouse mAb to LMP2, TAP1, TAP2 and LMP2 that are suitable for immunohistochemical analysis of normal and malignant tissues.
we have generated mAb specific for the LMP and TAp proteins and that the mAb react specifically with the corresponding antigens in immunoprecipitation and immunohistological studies.
we have developed mAb to LMP2, TAP1, TAP2 and LMP2 that are specific for these molecules in Western blotting, immunoprecipitation and immunohistochemistry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of reagents to analyze cellular and tissue expression of LMP and the TAP subunits in health and disease.
the development of mAb to LMP and TAp subunits, which can be used in immunological and molecular studies on the expression, structure and functions of these molecules.
developing mAb for the analysis of LMP2, TAP2 and TAP1 in human cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these mAbs will be valuable tools for studying the role of LMP and tapasin in antigen processing and presentation and in immune responses in general.
the antibodies are useful for immunohistochemistry and immunoprecipitation of LMP and Tap proteins.
these mAbs are useful tools for the characterization of LMP and/or TAP expression and distribution in normal and pathological conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed mAb that can be useful to investigate the role of LMP2 and LPM7 in the proteolytic processing of the invariant chain and TAP in the translocation of peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum.
we have developed and characterized four new mAb for the LMP2, the LMP7, the TAP1 and the TAP2 proteins.
we have developed and characterized mAb to LMP2, TAP1, TAP2 and LMP2, and that these reagents will be valuable for the analysis of LMP and the TAP system in human cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have generated a panel of mAb to LMP2, -7 and TAP1 and -2 subunits, which will be useful to analyze their expression and function in normal cells and in transformed cells.

the anti-LMP and TAP mAb we have generated can be used for the detection of these subunits in immunoprecipitation, ELISA, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and intracytoplasmatic staining reactions.
we have developed mAb that can be used to analyze the structure, expression, and function of LMP and Tap subunits in normal and transformed cell lines.
